thread:
Alex W.: Morning async — quick standup. What I did: started a canary to lower the batcher eviction threshold after yesterday's tail latency. Blocker: saw a brief 504 spike at ~03:10 UTC during canary, need traces. Today: triage alerts, update runbook, coordinate driver patch rollout.

Maria P.: I pulled traces. Spike aligns with a small batcher backlog and long GPU init on one node. Pushing a config tweak to reduce max_batch_wait from 12ms -> 8ms in canary.

Jordan C.: Oncall update: added a temporary 3-occurences/5m debounce to the 504 paging rule so we don't wake up the rotation for a 1-off blip. Rule id: SLO-HTTP-504.

Lee (SRE): Please annotate the alert when you add debounce so we know why it was muted. Also add any config diff to runbook.

Jordan C.: Command I ran (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/alerts/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -d '{"rule_id":"SLO-HTTP-504","debounce":3,"window":"5m","meta":{"ephemeral":true}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy completed: canary/evict-config v2 -> 3 hosts (build #4213) :shipit:

Alex W.: @Maria can you drop the datadog trace + logs link?

Maria P.: Trace: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/abc123 (sampling shows spike at 03:10). Logs: gs://redwood-logs/evict/2026-03-16/part-*.log. I also uploaded a short flamegraph to the shared folder.

Lee (SRE): Heads-up: vendor scheduled a driver security patch tonight 23:00 UTC; maintenance window planned. Oncall rotation and owner assigned.

oncall-bot: Pager rotation update: Jordan C. -> Maya S. starting 2026-03-17 00:00 UTC

Maya S.: Ack, I'll watch the canary through the maintenance window. If we see recurring 504s we should revert the change and escalate.

Alex W.: Action item: I will draft a runbook snippet for "504s correlated with batcher backlog" and link it here. If anyone has immediate notes about thresholds or previous mitigations, paste them.

Maria P.: Draft posted: https://redwood.runbooks/kv-batcher-backlog (pls review). Key note: prefer debounce + annotation over full suppression.

Lee (SRE): Agreed. Quick checklist: 1) annotate alert, 2) reduce max_batch_wait in canary, 3) monitor 5m error rate and batcher queue depth, 4) only escalate if sustained >5m.

Alex W.: Thanks — ping me if you want postmortem opened. I'll keep monitoring. :+1:
